column_values.text: In R4, the MVP portfolio workstream is focused on making WiseOS secure, reliable and ready to send updates back to Salesforce. The biggest piece is closing the security gaps found in the recent audit; most are already fixed and in testing, and the last few network and access fixes are underway. In parallel, the team is laying the groundwork for WiseOS to write meeting notes and follow-up tasks into Salesforce, starting with research and a test run in a Salesforce sandbox. Supporting work includes automating releases so updates reach advisors without manual steps, strengthening the data feeds behind the screens, and finishing the admin tools the team uses to spot and fix errors.

In R4, wiseAdvisor improves the advisor’s task list. Advisors will see an overdue count at a glance, a full task page they can sort and filter by type, who each task is for, and their own profile from the menu. Almost all of this is built and in testing. The last piece, making sure tasks for household members reach the whole client team, is in progress.
Data availability in DAP or RPT

In R4, wiseClient360 gives advisors a clearer picture of each household. Both spouses will show with ages and dates of birth, family members can be opened, and Portfolio tab accounts will be grouped the way Tamarac groups them. Several fixes are in testing, including sorting clients by last name and no longer listing clients’ children as prospects. Still in progress are the fee schedule and annual revenue on the client overview, early discovery on pulling Fidelity and Schwab data, and a fix to “last interaction” so it counts emails and calls, which is currently blocked.
Data availability and fidelity in DAP or RPT
Where to get last interaction date from or wait for RPT

In R4, wiseMeet makes meeting prep and recaps more complete and easier to act on. Advisors will see Outlook details on each meeting, a Join button, the client’s open Salesforce tasks, upcoming birthdays, account balances and follow-ups from past meetings. They’ll also be able to check off and edit recap action items. Most of this is built and in testing; the remaining pieces are prep templates for each meeting type and a firm-wide agenda structure, both waiting on a move to a new AI model.

In R4, wiseCoach makes coaching numbers more accurate and flexible. Advisors can pick their own date range, and shared books will now count correctly on Home and in WiseCoach; both are built and in testing. Referral suggestions tailored to an advisor’s level and client asset bands are planned but waiting on a business decision about the rules.
